edit.description: The home: two `pub(crate) const`s beside `MARKETPLACE_FIELD` (:223), whose own doc already states this pattern's reason — "the one home the SDK's edge declaration and the reference graph that resolves it both name, so the edge field and the value it reads cannot drift apart". Name them for the SDK's own pair so the seam reads one vocabulary: `HOOK_HANDLER_KEY` = `hooks` (the key a matcher group carries its handler array under) and `HOOK_MATCHER_KEY` = `matcher` (the one field lifted beside it), each carrying the SDK's cite at the point of claim (`sdk/src/builtins.ts`:507,:511 — code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, "Matcher patterns", retrieved 2026-09-29). The first in-file consumer is the legacy-lock normalization at :932-:933, which restates both literals to reconstruct the shape a lock written before the `entry_shape` column carried implicitly. `CollectionKeyPath::HooksEvent.collection_key()` (:234) already owns the OUTER settings key and does not move.

The `hook` built-in's `EntryShape::GroupArray` at :300-:301 — the declaration every other site in the tree is a copy of — names the two constants instead of its literals. The in-crate unit test at :1076-:1077 asserts the same pair: name the constant on the declaration side only and leave the assertion's expected value spelled out, since a constant on both sides of an `assert_eq!` proves nothing about the wire.

Nine spellings over two concepts, neither of them install's to name. The handler-array key (`HOOK_HANDLER_KEY`): `session_start_group` (:2090) builds `{hooks:[{type,command}]}`, `group_has_command` (:2129) reads it back off one group, `gate_hook_fields` (:2510) authors the pair a scaffolded gate member carries. The lifted field (`HOOK_MATCHER_KEY`): `group_binds_matcher` (:2122) — d96975bb's new leaf question — and `gate_hook_fields` (:2507). The OUTER settings key already has a home this file does not use, `CollectionKeyPath::HooksEvent.collection_key()` (`src/kind.rs`:234, "the one place the wire key paths map to their manifest object, so the adapter's walk names no literal of its own"), while `fresh_settings` (:2010), `merge_settings` (:2056,:2074) and `event_has_group` (:2110) each spell `hooks` raw. Both folds land here; the second is the one the existing home was written for. Non-identity, expected untouched: `member_dir`'s `"hook" => "hooks"` (:2154) is the scaffold subdirectory name, not a wire key.

The read/write face takes `member_key` and `lifted_fields` as parameters and names no literal of its own — already correct, and the shape the rest folds toward. Only its unit tests restate the pair: the `EntryShape::GroupArray` fixture (:1220-:1221) and the driving arguments to `manifest_members` (:1137,:1182,:1218) and `hook_matcher_group` (:1250,:1266-:1267,:1283). Name the constants on those driving sides and keep every wire-shaped expectation literal (:1202-:1210, :1230, :1233, :1272-:1273, :1284), the same reason as the built-in's test. The `e.g., "hooks"` / `["matcher"]` examples in the two doc comments (:752,:754 and :812,:813) stay prose — they illustrate the generic face's parameters, not a spelling it depends on.

Two `"hooks"` spellings, both expected untouched and both declared here so the acceptance census closes: `hooks_manifest` (:285) keys the plugin's own `hooks/hooks.json` top-level object — a different manifest's schema, not this key — and the unit test at :424 walks `hooks["hooks"]["SessionStart"][0]["hooks"][0]`, whose INNER key is this entry's handler-array one. Unlike `tests/it/**`, an in-crate unit test can see a `pub(crate)` const, so the ruling is declared rather than left to the fence: a wire-pinning assertion stays literal, the same reason as the built-in's test.

Listed for the fence, expected untouched: the integration crate cannot see a `pub(crate)` constant, and its assertions read the bytes install actually wrote, so they stay literal by design (`engineering.md`, "A seam gate reads what the real writer wrote"). Widening the constant to `pub` to reach here is the wrong move — "An export earns its consumer", and the consumer is in-crate.

Listed for the fence, expected untouched, same reason: the hook read/write round-trip over a real manifest drives the wire bytes and asserts them literally. The fold changes no behavior, so a green run here is the acceptance, not a site to edit.

summary: One home for the hook group's wire keys — `hooks` and `matcher` are bare literals at nine install sites plus two declarations, while the SDK names each exactly once.

tests.asserts: the `hook` kind's collection address still pins the `hooks`/`matcher` group-array spelling, with the expectation side spelled literally
install's settings merge and its gate-hook scaffold write byte-identical output — the fold changes no behavior
the hook read/write round-trip over a real manifest stays green
the plugin's `hooks/hooks.json` manifest still carries the engine's SessionStart command inside its handler array, the assertion spelled literally

acceptance: cargo test green, clippy/fmt clean, and `rg '"hooks"|"matcher"' src/` resolves to the two constants' definitions plus only the named non-identities: `src/kind.rs`:234's `collection_key()` (the outer settings key's own home), `src/install.rs`:2154's `member_dir` scaffold directory, `src/bundle.rs`:285's plugin `hooks/hooks.json` top-level key, the two `json_manifest.rs` doc-comment examples, the wire-pinning assertions in three unit tests (`src/builtin_kind.rs`, `src/json_manifest.rs`, `src/bundle.rs`:424), and `src/builtin_lock.toml`'s three `field = "hooks"` clause rows (:763, :897, :1081 — plugin-manifest's path field twice and settings-local's hooks object, none of them this key; that file is byte-derived from the SDK under `tests/it/builtin_lock_frozen.rs`, never a hand-spelled site).
notes: The second half of the HOOK-AUTHORS fence capture; its gating reason is discharged — 402bfe32 and d96975bb landed, so `gate_hook_fields` and its neighbours stopped moving. Every cite re-censused at HEAD: install.rs went from six sites to nine (`event_has_command` retired for `event_has_group`, `group_binds_matcher` new), and the SDK's own pair names the consts. scoped at 2cbe66ac
